To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. IT chemotherapy is a useful treatment modality in selected cases of solid malignancies with CNS involvement; 2. IT chemotherapy is associated with significant toxicity, particularly neurotoxicity; 3. IT chemotherapy should be administered only by an expert multidisciplinary team.

(1) the incidence of neurotoxicity is higher with IT chemotherapy compared with systemic chemotherapy; (2) IT chemotherapy is associated with an increased risk of developing a secondary malignancy; (3) the risk of secondary malignancy is higher with IT therapy than with systemic chemotherapy; and (4) there is a lack of evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of intraventricular chemotherapy.
1) The use of IT chemotherapy in the treatment of leptomeningeal metastases is not supported by the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of intrathecal chemotherapy drugs for the treatment of malignant and benign diseases of the central nervous system.
the use of IT methotrexate (MTX) for the treatment of central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma and leptomeningeal carcinomatosis.
the role of the IT route for the delivery of anticancer agents in children and adults.
